Incidents Bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: Sungrove (dedicated pool, VPC) high tail latency + partial 5xx spike since ~10:12 UTC. Pager: maria.k@redwood.com.

Alex R.: I'm here, grabbing logs and the current scheduler config. Any customer-facing impact?

Maria K.: Sungrove reported timeouts from their API (client-side) and we see 95p latency > 6s on their tenant queue. Error rate ~3% 500s, mostly inference-timeouts. They are on a dedicated pool with bespoke batch settings.

Sanjay P.: Copy. Checking the tenant shard: pool-dedicated-us-west-3, tenant_id=sg-7721. Current max_batch_tokens=4096 per tenant override, scheduler.max_batch_tokens global=8192.

Leo T.: Who last touched Sungrove overrides?

Nina (SRE): Last change was a week ago by product for throughput during peak testing. They used aggressive max_batch_tokens + high batch delay to favor throughput.

Alex R.: Ok, hypothesis: too-large max_batch_tokens + long batch window -> long queueing for a single tenant causing head-of-line latency and occasional OOM/rejections on worker nodes when their bursts coincide. We should: 1) temporarily reduce tenant max_batch_tokens, 2) tighten scheduler batching window / reduce max_wait_ms for that tenant, 3) enable queue isolation (soft limit) to prevent cross-tenant interference.

Maria K.: Agreed. Also consider routing Sungrove to a smaller model variant for a short window if kernels are saturated. But prioritize queue knobs first.

Sanjay P.: Running `redwoodctl tenant get sg-7721 --overrides` to fetch overrides...

Sanjay P.: Output:
```
{
  "tenant_id": "sg-7721",
  "overrides": {
    "max_batch_tokens": "4096",
    "batch_delay_ms": "80",
    "queue_share": "1.0",
    "model_variant": "gpt-small-opt"
  }
}
```

Alex R.: Plan: step 1 (fast rollback) set tenant override max_batch_tokens=1024 and batch_delay_ms=20. step 2 add queue_share=0.5 to limit capacity hog. step 3 observe for 3-5m and escalate to model fallback if not improving.

Leo T.: I'm on infra. If we change max_batch_tokens, confirm there is no in-flight KV-cache mismatch for the worker nodes. Might need to restart a subset of workers if we see desync.

Maria K.: I'll message Sungrove CSM + SE: "we're applying a temporary queue/shaper change to reduce tail latency; no code changes required on your side."

DeployBot: Applying override for tenant sg-7721: setting max_batch_tokens=1024, batch_delay_ms=20, queue_share=0.5.

DeployBot: Change applied (config version 2026-03-15T10:28:34Z). No rolling restart required for config-only change.

Alex R.: Running realtime metrics: `metrics query latency_percentiles{tenant=\"sg-7721\"}`

Alex R.: Before change 95p=6.1s, 99p=12.3s. After change (t+90s): 95p=1.2s, 99p=2.8s. Error rate down to 0.4%. Looks promising.

Nina (SRE): Observed per-worker memory: one worker had transient GC spikes coincident with Sungrove bursts. Noted but not OOM. Queue depth for sg-7721 dropped from 420 to ~70.

Sanjay P.: Reverted the temporary queue_share back to 0.8 after initial stabilization to prevent throttling below their SLA. Current tenant overrides now: max_batch_tokens=1024, batch_delay_ms=25, queue_share=0.8.

Maria K.: Sungrove SE confirms decreased client timeouts. They saw a drop in 500s and improved p99. They asked what changed. I'll send them the summary and ETA for finish.

Alex R.: Followups: 1) Need a runbook entry for "tenant large-batch surge" describing safe bounds for max_batch_tokens per pool size. 2) Add automated alert that fires when a single tenant consumes >40% of pool tokens for >2m. 3) Consider default tenant isolation profiles for dedicated pools (soft/strict modes).

Leo T.: I'll open infra ticket for telemetry: add per-tenant token utilization metric and alarm.

Maria K.: I'll schedule a post-incident meeting with Sungrove and their SE next week. Also flag for product to revisit the override UI so it's clearer the cost/latency tradeoffs.

Sanjay P.: Notes for postmortem: root cause = oversized tenant batch override + long batch_delay leading to head-of-line queueing and transient worker GC spikes. Mitigations = temporary reduction in max_batch_tokens and batch_delay_ms, partial queue_share throttle, monitoring + alerting.

Alex R.: Closing action: Nina to watch for 1h, if p99 stays under 3s and error rate <1% we'll mark mitigated. I'll create the incident doc and link metrics graphs.

Nina (SRE): Watching. Current status: mitigated -> under observation. :white_check_mark:

Incidents Bot: Incident status -> mitigated (2026-03-15T10:37:20Z).

Maria K.: Thanks team. Leaving handoff note for next on-call: continue watch for 2 hours, avoid rolling restarts unless OOMs recur.

Alex R.: Thanks all. End thread.
